d: HSBC aims to be the international bank of choice for affluent customers, supporting their domestic and international banking, and holistic wealth management needs. We help customers to take care of their day-to-day finances and to manage, protect and grow their wealth. Our international network and breadth of expertise enable us to support individuals, families, business owners, investors and entrepreneurs around the world.

The Open Market Advisor drives NTB acquisition, revolving and borrowing results through need-based selling. They manage company relationships, support employees with banking needs, improve HSBC’s penetration and refer suitable customers to specialist businesses.
q: Strong knowledge of retail banking products and propositions, including salary accounts, borrowing, revolving credit, co-branded cards, wealth and international banking solutions.
Proven experience in acquiring new-to-bank accounts through employer relationships, company visits, employee engagement and self-generated leads.
Proven sales experience, including co-branded card sales, with the ability to identify customer needs, explain product benefits and achieve agreed acquisition, activation and cross-sell targets.
Strong lead-generation, pipeline-management and communication skills, with the ability to build networks, manage customer contacts, use CRM systems and deliver effective referrals and handovers.

Knowledge of customer service, risk and compliance requirements, including fair dealing, internal controls, anti-money-laundering standards, complaint resolution and maintaining high-quality processing.

A full-time graduation degree of at least three years is essential for obtaining a UAE visa and work permit. For degrees obtained outside the UAE, valid attestations and equivalency are also mandatory.

HSBC is committed to building a culture where all employees are valued, respected and opinions count. We take pride in providing a workplace that fosters continuous professional development, flexible work and opportunities to grow within an inclusive and diverse environment.

We believe diversity brings benefits for our customers, our business and our people. Different ideas and perspectives help us innovate, manage risk and grow the business in a sustainable way. Personal data held by the Bank relating to employment applications will be used in accordance with our Privacy Statement, which is available on our website.
Issued by The Hong Kong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited.
r: Deliver business performance: Maximize business opportunities within the assigned companies. Meet targets across acquisition (excluding Premier), Revolving Credit, Borrowing. Build long-term relationships with key contacts within assigned Open Market portfolio. Identify new business opportunities within and work closely with Open market Sales Manager to drive acquisition and cross-sell
Manage assigned company relationships: Act as the primary banking contact for employees of assigned companies and build long-term relationships with key company contacts.
Identify and develop business opportunities: Maximize opportunities within assigned and non-Approved Employee List companies, working with Sales Managers to drive acquisition and cross-selling.

Understand customer needs and make referrals: Use the EDRAS (Engage, Discover, Recommend, Act and Service) need-based selling methodology and refer suitable customers to Wealth, International Banking Corridors and Private Banking.
Provide personalized customer service: Manage customer expectations, promote digital services, act as an HSBC Service Ambassador and resolve complaints within the required SLA.

Maintain activity, quality and compliance standards: Ensure compliance with internal and external regulations such as with Group policies on compliance and money laundering deterrence, contain risk within the team and reinforce/ strengthen the HSBC Money Laundering and Compliance policy.

d: We are seeking a professional, customer-focused, and highly motivated Remote Customer Experience Representative to join our team. The successful candidate will serve as the primary point of contact for customers, providing exceptional support, addressing inquiries, resolving complaints, and ensuring a positive customer experience across multiple communication channels.

As a Customer Service Representative, you will be responsible for assisting customers with questions about our products and services, processing requests, troubleshooting basic issues, handling complaints, and providing accurate information in a timely and professional manner.

The ideal candidate should have excellent communication and interpersonal skills, a strong problem-solving ability, patience, attention to detail, and the ability to work independently in a remote environment. You should be comfortable using computers, customer relationship management (CRM) systems, email platforms, live chat applications, and other digital communication tools.

This position requires someone who is passionate about helping people, capable of managing multiple customer inquiries, and committed to maintaining high standards of customer satisfaction and service quality.
Respond promptly and professionally to customer inquiries through phone calls, emails, live chat, and other approved communication channels.
Provide accurate information regarding company products, services, policies, procedures, pricing, and account-related questions.
Listen carefully to customers to understand their needs, concerns, and expectations.
Maintain a friendly, patient, and professional attitude when interacting with customers.
Guide customers through processes, account updates, product usage, and general service inquiries.
Follow up with customers when necessary to ensure their concerns have been properly addressed.
Identify customer concerns and provide appropriate solutions in a timely and effective manner.
Handle customer complaints, disputes, and service-related issues with empathy and professionalism.
De-escalate difficult conversations and manage dissatisfied customers while maintaining a positive customer experience.
Investigate reported issues and coordinate with relevant departments to resolve complex problems.
Escalate unresolved or sensitive matters to the appropriate supervisor or department.
Take ownership of customer issues and ensure proper follow-through until resolution.
Assist customers with placing orders, tracking shipments, processing cancellations, and managing returns or exchanges, where applicable.
Help customers update personal information, account details, subscriptions, and service preferences.
Verify customer information and maintain accurate records of interactions and transactions.
Provide updates regarding order status, service requests, refunds, and other account-related matters.
Ensure that all customer requests are handled according to company policies and established procedures.
Record customer interactions, inquiries, complaints, and resolutions accurately in the company's CRM or customer support system.
Maintain organized and up-to-date customer records.
Document recurring issues, customer feedback, and frequently reported concerns.
Prepare reports on customer interactions, service requests, and unresolved cases when required.
Ensure that all customer information is handled confidentially and in accordance with company data protection policies.
Build positive relationships with customers through attentive, personalized, and reliable support.
Identify opportunities to improve customer satisfaction and strengthen customer loyalty.
Educate customers about relevant products, services, features, and available solutions.
Collect customer feedback and communicate suggestions for improving products and services.
Represent the company positively in every customer interaction.
Work toward achieving customer satisfaction, first-contact resolution, and service quality targets.
Collaborate with other customer service representatives, supervisors, and internal departments to resolve customer concerns.
Participate in virtual team meetings, training sessions, and performance reviews.
Stay informed about company policies, product updates, service changes, and customer support procedures.
Follow established workflows, service standards, and communication guidelines.
Identify opportunities to improve customer service processes and operational efficiency.
Demonstrate flexibility and willingness to take on additional responsibilities when required.
q: High school diploma or equivalent qualification required.
Additional education, training, or certification in customer service, business administration, communications, or a related field is an advantage.
Previous experience in customer service, call center operations, sales support, client relations, or a similar role is preferred.
Experience working with customers through phone, email, and live chat is an advantage.
Familiarity with CRM software, help desk platforms, and customer support tools is beneficial.
Candidates with strong communication skills and a willingness to learn may also be considered for entry-level opportunities.
Proficiency in using computers, email applications, web browsers, and Microsoft Office or Google Workspace.
Ability to navigate multiple software applications and digital platforms efficiently.
Familiarity with CRM systems such as Salesforce, HubSpot, Zendesk, or Freshdesk is an advantage.
Ability to type accurately and manage multiple customer requests simultaneously.
Basic troubleshooting and digital problem-solving skills.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
Strong active listening and comprehension abilities.
Ability to explain information clearly and communicate effectively with people from different backgrounds.
Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to establish positive customer relationships.
Fluency in the required working language(s).
The Ideal Candidate Should Demonstrate The Following Qualities
Customer-focused: Genuine interest in helping customers and ensuring their satisfaction.
Patient and empathetic: Ability to remain calm, understanding, and respectful when dealing with frustrated or demanding customers.
Problem-solver: Strong analytical thinking and the ability to identify practical solutions.
Reliable and accountable: Consistently meets deadlines, follows procedures, and takes responsibility for assigned tasks.
Detail-oriented: Ensures accuracy when documenting information, processing requests, and communicating with customers.
Organized: Able to prioritize tasks and manage multiple customer inquiries efficiently.
Adaptable: Comfortable learning new technologies, processes, and company policies.
Self-motivated: Able to work independently and remain productive without constant supervision.
Team player: Willing to collaborate, share knowledge, and contribute to team objectives.
Professional: Maintains confidentiality, integrity, and a positive attitude at all times.
Since this is a fully remote position, candidates must have the ability to work effectively from home and maintain a professional working environment.
A functional laptop or desktop computer that meets company technical requirements.
A working headset with a microphone, particularly for roles involving phone support.
A quiet, distraction-free workspace suitable for professional customer interactions.
Basic knowledge of online communication and collaboration tools such as Zoom, Microsoft Teams, or Slack.
Ability to manage working hours, meet deadlines, and maintain productivity independently.
Availability to attend virtual meetings, training sessions, and scheduled team check-ins.
Ability to comply with company security requirements and protect confidential customer information.
Performance Expectations and Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)
The Customer Service Representative will be evaluated based on measurable performance indicators, including:
Customer Satisfaction Score (CSAT): Maintaining high customer satisfaction through professional and effective support.
First Contact Resolution (FCR): Resolving customer concerns during the initial interaction whenever possible.
Response Time: Responding to customer inquiries within established service-level targets.
Average Handling Time (AHT): Managing customer interactions efficiently without compromising service quality.
Quality Assurance Score: Maintaining accuracy, professionalism, and compliance with company communication standards.

d: PayLink is seeking a Risk Manager to lead its Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) function as an independent control function. You will develop and maintain the risk management framework, assess risks across the business, and provide clear insights that support informed decisions, business resilience, and compliance with applicable Saudi Central Bank (SAMA) requirements.
The role works closely with senior management, relevant committees, and departmental risk owners while maintaining independent oversight and clear accountability.
q: Bachelor’s degree in Risk Management, Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, or a related discipline; a postgraduate qualification is preferred.
Preferably at least seven years of relevant experience in risk management, governance, or financial services, including leadership experience, subject to applicable fit-and-proper requirements.
Practical experience within financial institutions or payment service providers supervised by the Saudi Central Bank (SAMA).

Working knowledge of Enterprise Risk Management (ERM), Risk and Control Self-Assessments (RCSA), risk appetite, Key Risk Indicators (KRIs), Business Continuity Management (BCM), internal controls, and regulatory reporting.
Relevant professional credentials, such as FRM, CRMP, RIMS-CRMP, or an ISO 31000-related qualification, are preferred and complement practical experience.
Strong analytical judgment and independent assessment skills, with the ability to connect risk exposures to business objectives and regulatory impact.
Effective communication, cross-functional coordination, and professional conflict management skills.
Ability to prepare clear executive reports and provide practical, actionable recommendations.
Strong planning and prioritization skills, including tracking remediation activities within available resources.
Ability to evaluate evidence and data while maintaining the confidentiality of sensitive information.
Leadership and coaching skills, with the ability to strengthen risk culture and influence stakeholders without direct line authority.
r: Governance, Strategy and Risk Management Framework
Develop and update the Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) framework, policies, methodologies, tools and templates, and submit them for approval under the delegation of authority.
Prepare an annual risk management strategy and work plan aligned with the Company’s strategy, license category and scale of operations.
Define roles, responsibilities, escalation lines, risk owners and control owners in coordination with relevant departments, without imposing unapproved operational authority.
Support the Risk Committee and relevant committees by preparing materials and reports and tracking decisions within each committee’s mandate.
Review the framework periodically following product, business model or regulatory changes or material events.
Risk Identification, Assessment and Risk Register
Lead enterprise assessments of inherent and residual risk in collaboration with departmental risk owners.
Establish and maintain the enterprise risk register, documenting causes, impacts, controls, assessments, treatment owners and target dates.
Coordinate Risk and Control Self-Assessments (RCSA) and challenge the reasonableness of assessments against available evidence.
Assess enterprise risks arising from new products and services, material changes, projects, expansion and partnerships before recommendations are submitted.
Conduct scenario analyses and stress testing in line with priorities, capabilities and available data, in coordination with Finance, Operations and Technology.

Develop and review the risk appetite statement and tolerance limits in coordination with Finance, Compliance, Operations, Cybersecurity and other stakeholders, and submit them to the authorized approving body.
Develop a proportionate set of Key Risk Indicators (KRIs), defining data sources, data owners, measurement frequency and alert thresholds.
Monitor risk appetite breaches, analyze their causes, recommend mitigation and escalate under approved authorities.
Produce concise periodic reports for senior management and relevant committees on material risks, trends, breaches, remediation plans and decisions required.
Assess control design adequacy and effectiveness from a risk management perspective, using supporting evidence, test results, reports, interviews and appropriate samples.
Request information and evidence necessary for risk assessments within approved access rights, need-to-know principles, confidentiality and data protection requirements.
Document professional disagreements with risk or control owners and escalate material matters through approved channels.
Do not operate controls, make specialist operational decisions or substitute for Internal Audit’s independent assurance role.
Financial, Operational, Technology and Financial Crime Risks
Monitor risks relating to liquidity, settlements, partner banks, fraud, operations, third parties, concentration, reputation and strategy in coordination with their respective owners.
Assess cybersecurity and technology risks within the enterprise framework in coordination with Cybersecurity and Technology, without assuming their specialist or operational responsibilities.

Include money laundering, terrorist financing and proliferation financing risks in the enterprise risk register and independently challenge exposures, controls and residual risk in coordination with Compliance and the AML officer.

Access appropriate transaction, alert and suspicion-related indicators for risk assessment, subject to confidentiality restrictions on reports and protected case files; this role does not include investigating individual cases or making regulatory reporting decisions.
Ensure enterprise assessments align with specialist risk assessments without creating conflicting assessments or transferring ownership of specialist programs to Risk Management.
Oversee the Business Continuity Management (BCM) framework and program through the Business Continuity Officer and relevant functions, monitoring plans, testing and remediation readiness.
Review Business Impact Analysis (BIA) results, verify business owners’ validation of impacts and dependencies, and confirm that Technology and Operations have assessed recovery target feasibility.
Monitor business continuity, disaster recovery and crisis management plans and tests, while operational response and recovery remain with designated teams.
Report material readiness gaps to senior management and relevant committees, coordinating with Compliance on regulatory notifications.
Assess risks relating to suppliers, outsourcing, third-party dependencies, concentration and single points of failure in collaboration with relationship owners.
Review risks associated with projects, material changes and new services and provide recommendations before approval.
Track risk mitigation plans, action owners and deadlines without executing other departments’ remedial actions.
Monitor regulatory requirements applicable to the risk management function and compile supporting evidence with Compliance and relevant stakeholders.
Participate in supervisory visits and respond on enterprise risk management topics using validated information, referring specialist technical topics to their owners.
Track regulatory and Internal Audit findings relevant to Risk Management and verify remediation by responsible owners.
Deliver practical risk awareness and training to risk owners and promote risk culture throughout the Company.
Maintain orderly records of evidence, assessments, reports, decisions and relevant correspondence.

d: Established in the 1930s, Al-Futtaim is one of the most diversified and progressive privately held regional businesses, headquartered in Dubai. Operating across more than 20 countries, the Group spans automotive, financial services, real estate, retail and health. With more than 40,000 employees, Al-Futtaim represents over 200 of the world’s most recognised brands, including Toyota, Lexus, IKEA, ACE and Marks & Spencer. Driven by its purpose to enrich lives and elevate communities, Al-Futtaim focuses on digital innovation, AI, sustainable growth and strategic partnerships, creating long-term value for customers, communities and partners while building a responsible legacy for future generations.

As a Visual Merchandising Assistant at Marks and Spencer, you will be responsible for implementing and maintaining the M&S brand image within the store ensuring visual consistency. Your role involves working alongside the Senior Visual Merchandiser and Commercial Managers to provide customers with an inspirational shopping experience. You will be part of the in-store visual merchandising team, executing merchandising strategies by designing, developing, and maintaining visual displays both in store windows and on the sales floor. You will have a substantial impact on marketing, advertising, and contributing to the profitability of the store through effective merchandise handling, replenishment, and inventory control.
q: Strong visual merchandising and styling skills.
Excellent communication skills with ability to liaise with retail staff and management.
Ability to manage time effectively and ensure timely implementation of visual strategies.
Keen awareness of fashion trends and competitor analysis.
What Qualifies You For The Role
3 years of experience in a Visual Merchandising position within a fashion retail brand.
Ability to communicate with retail staff at all levels.
Ability to read and carry out clear instructions for guidelines implementation.

At Al-Futtaim Retail, we are part of a 90-year legacy built on ambition, progress and long-term vision. As one of the region’s leading retail operators, we partner with some of the world’s most trusted brands – including IKEA, ACE, Marks & Spencer and the Inditex Group – bringing global excellence to customers across MENA and Southeast Asia.

We don’t just operate stores; we shape retail experiences. From launching brands like Watsons and Kiabi to our regions for the first time, to investing in digital innovation, AI capabilities, the customer experience and loyalty platforms, we are constantly redefining the future of retail.

With over 100 nationalities spread across more than 10 countries, our strength lies in our diverse and collaborative community. Here, you’re equipped to turn your ambition into action, building the career you want, while helping us move retail forwards.
Join us and be part of The Heart of Tomorrow.
r: Follow the Visual Merchandising Guidelines and ensure these are rolled out across the store.
Implement mannequins styled in line with the styling policy.
Use appropriate styling techniques and correct visual elements for customer segmentation.
Collaborate with Senior Visual Merchandisers and store teams to implement seasonal launches and events on time and on brand.
Maintain awareness of competitor activities and trends within visual merchandising.
Ensure brand consistency through educating and training sales staff to keep visual merchandising in line with standards.
Maintain and adhere to the merchandising checklist.
Liaise daily with the Visual Merchandiser for updates on processes and requirements.
Contribute to the profitability of the store with merchandise handling, replenishment, and inventory control efforts.
Take charge of designing and developing visual displays in store windows and on the sales floor.
